# Single-cell GEX: cell states and clonal programmes {#sec-sc-gex}

Every receptor joined to its cell's transcriptional state, from the annotated GEX object
(`--input_annotated_object`). A repertoire alone says *that* a clone expanded; with the
transcriptome it also says *what the expanded cells are*: effector, memory, exhausted or
proliferating. The questions here are which states carry the expansion, what happens to the
cells of clones that grow or shrink over time, which clones span several states, what the
expanded cells express, and where CoNGA and TCRi place them. The section is also published on
its own as `SC_GEX_Report.html`. Run-level checks of the receptor-to-cell join are in the
**QC & Run Info** report (T-cell integration), and how often each clustering method covers each
state is in the **Details: Patient** report (clustering coverage by cell state).

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" collapse="true"}
## Key terms
- **Clone**: cells sharing the same paired α/β receptor, the progeny of one naive T cell.
- **Cell state**: the cell's annotation from the GEX object.
- **Expanded**: a clone with at least 2 cells *in the same sample*. Proliferation follows antigen
  recognition, so expanded clones are the best candidates for antigen-specific T cells.
- **Sample labels**: samples are shown by their samplesheet `alias` (for example
  `P001_d0_L1`) where one is given, otherwise by the library name.
:::

```{r}
#| label: gex-load
# Per-cell table: the T-cell integration export (cell state, clone, embedding), with the
# CoNGA, TCRi and consensus per-cell calls joined on cell_id.
gx <- T("tcell", "tcr_export_cells_with_embedding.tsv")
gx_by_id <- function(module, name, keep) {
  d <- T(module, name)
  if (!have(d) || !"cell_id" %in% names(d)) return(NULL)
  keep <- intersect(keep, names(d))
  if (!length(keep)) return(NULL)
  d <- d[, c("cell_id", keep), drop = FALSE]
  d$cell_id <- as.character(d$cell_id)
  d[!duplicated(d$cell_id), , drop = FALSE]
}
if (have(gx)) {
  gx$cell_id <- as.character(gx$cell_id)
  for (j in list(
    gx_by_id("conga", "conga_export_cells.tsv", c("conga_score", "conga_gex_cluster", "conga_tcr_cluster")),
    gx_by_id("tcri", "tcri_export_cells.tsv", c("tcri_score", "tcri_group", "tcri_predicted_phenotype")),
    gx_by_id("consensus", "consensus_export_cells.tsv", c("consensus_cluster")))) {
    if (!is.null(j)) gx <- left_join(gx[, setdiff(names(gx), setdiff(names(j), "cell_id")), drop = FALSE],
                                     j, by = "cell_id")
  }
  gx$annot   <- if ("annot" %in% names(gx)) as.character(gx$annot) else "Unannotated"
  gx$annot[is.na(gx$annot) | !nzchar(gx$annot)] <- "Unannotated"
  gx$has_tcr <- if ("has_tcr" %in% names(gx)) toupper(as.character(gx$has_tcr)) %in% c("TRUE", "T", "1") else !is.na(gx$clone_id)
  # The export's clone_size counts a clone across the whole cohort; expansion is judged
  # within a sample, so recount there.
  gx$clone_id[!gx$has_tcr] <- NA
  gx <- gx %>% group_by(sample, clone_id) %>%
    mutate(clone_size = ifelse(is.na(clone_id), NA_real_, as.numeric(n()))) %>% ungroup() %>%
    as.data.frame()
  gx$size_bin <- ifelse(!gx$has_tcr | is.na(gx$clone_size), "no TCR",
                 as.character(cut(gx$clone_size, c(0, 1, 2, 5, 20, Inf),
                                  labels = c("1 cell", "2 cells", "3-5 cells", "6-20 cells", ">20 cells"))))
  gx$expanded <- gx$has_tcr & !is.na(gx$clone_size) & gx$clone_size >= 2
  emb <- grep("^(umap|u|UMAP)_?[12]$", names(gx), value = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)
  gx_emb <- if (length(emb) >= 2) emb[1:2] else NULL
  gx_cond <- intersect(c("condition"), names(gx))
  gx_cond <- if (length(gx_cond) && n_distinct_real(gx[[gx_cond]]) >= 2) gx_cond else NULL
}
# Patient, timepoint order, compartment, alias and CDR3b for the longitudinal and dynamics views.
gx_pcol <- if (have(gx)) intersect(c(as_str1(params$patient_col), "patient", "patient_id"), names(gx))[1] else NA
tp_order <- trimws(strsplit(as_str1(params$timepoint_order), ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1]])
tp_order <- tp_order[nzchar(tp_order)]
cd_clono <- T("clonal", "clonotypes.csv")
if (have(gx)) {
  gx$patient_ <- if (!is.na(gx_pcol)) as.character(gx[[gx_pcol]]) else "all"
  # Sample metadata from the samplesheet, carried by CLONAL_DYNAMICS: compartment, alias and
  # timepoint. The GEX object does not always hold the timepoint, so the samplesheet's fills
  # any cell that lacks one.
  smap <- if (have(cd_clono) && "sample" %in% names(cd_clono))
    cd_clono[!duplicated(cd_clono$sample), intersect(c("sample", "origin", "alias", "timepoint"), names(cd_clono)), drop = FALSE] else NULL
  from_sheet <- function(col) if (!is.null(smap) && col %in% names(smap))
    as.character(smap[[col]][match(gx$sample, smap$sample)]) else rep(NA_character_, nrow(gx))
  if (!"timepoint" %in% names(gx)) gx$timepoint <- NA_character_
  gx$timepoint <- as.character(gx$timepoint)
  miss <- is.na(gx$timepoint) | !nzchar(gx$timepoint)
  gx$timepoint[miss] <- from_sheet("timepoint")[miss]
  gx$origin <- from_sheet("origin")
  gx$origin[is.na(gx$origin) | !nzchar(gx$origin)] <- "all"
  gx$alias <- from_sheet("alias")
  no_alias <- is.na(gx$alias) | !nzchar(gx$alias)
  gx$alias[no_alias] <- as.character(gx$sample[no_alias])
  tps <- unique(as.character(gx$timepoint)); tps <- tps[!is.na(tps) & nzchar(tps)]
  gx_tp_levels <- c(intersect(tp_order, tps), sort(setdiff(tps, tp_order)))
  # Samples by patient, then timepoint, then compartment: the order of every per-sample axis.
  gx_samples <- gx %>% distinct(sample, alias, patient_, timepoint, origin) %>%
    distinct(sample, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(tpr = match(timepoint, gx_tp_levels)) %>% arrange(patient_, tpr, origin, alias)
  gx_samples$alias <- make.unique(gx_samples$alias)
  gx$alias <- gx_samples$alias[match(gx$sample, gx_samples$sample)]
  gx_alias_levels <- gx_samples$alias
  gx$cdr3b <- if ("cdr3b" %in% names(gx)) as.character(gx$cdr3b) else sub("^.*B:", "", as.character(gx$clone_id))
  gx$conga_hit <- if ("conga_score" %in% names(gx)) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(gx$conga_score)) < 1 else NA
}
gx_tcr <- if (have(gx)) gx[gx$has_tcr, , drop = FALSE] else NULL
size_levels <- c("1 cell", "2 cells", "3-5 cells", "6-20 cells", ">20 cells", "no TCR")
size_cols   <- c("#a6a6a6", "#9ecae1", "#4292c6", "#08519c", "#de2d26", "#ececec")
state_cols  <- function(x) {
  lv <- sort(unique(as.character(x)))
  setNames(grDevices::colorRampPalette(c(pal, "#4d4d4d", "#b15928", "#6a3d9a", "#ff7f00"))(length(lv)), lv)
}

# Numbered caption under a figure or table of this section ("Figure G1."), counted only when
# the figure is drawn. text is HTML.
gx_fig_n <- 0; gx_tab_n <- 0
withcap <- function(w, title, text = "", kind = "Figure") {
  if (kind == "Figure") { gx_fig_n <<- gx_fig_n + 1; n <- gx_fig_n } else { gx_tab_n <<- gx_tab_n + 1; n <- gx_tab_n }
  # Inside a tagList a plotly widget takes the chunk's default height, not its layout's, and
  # the caption below would overlap a taller figure: size the widget from its layout.
  if (inherits(w, "plotly")) {
    w <- plotly::plotly_build(w)
    if (!is.null(w$x$layout$height)) w$height <- w$x$layout$height
    # A built bar trace would also print its hover text on the bar.
    w$x$data <- lapply(w$x$data, function(t) { if (identical(t$type, "bar")) t$textposition <- "none"; t })
  }
  htmltools::tagList(w, htmltools::tags$p(style = "margin-top: 0.5rem;",
    htmltools::HTML(sprintf("<strong>%s G%d. %s.</strong> %s", kind, n, title, text))))
}

# Heatmap. m: numeric matrix with dimnames; hover text from fmt, or a matrix of hover text.
hmap <- function(m, title, zlab, colorscale = "Viridis", height = 520, zmid = NULL, fmt = "%{z:.2f}",
                 text = NULL, zmin = NULL, zmax = NULL) {
  p <- if (is.null(text))
    plotly::plot_ly(x = colnames(m), y = rownames(m), z = m, type = "heatmap",
                    colorscale = colorscale, zmid = zmid, zmin = zmin, zmax = zmax,
                    colorbar = list(title = zlab),
                    hovertemplate = paste0("%{y} / %{x}<br>", zlab, ": ", fmt, "<extra></extra>"))
  else
    plotly::plot_ly(x = colnames(m), y = rownames(m), z = m, type = "heatmap",
                    colorscale = colorscale, zmid = zmid, zmin = zmin, zmax = zmax,
                    colorbar = list(title = zlab), text = text, hoverinfo = "text")
  pconf(plotly::layout(p, title = ttl(title), height = height,
                       margin = list(l = 140, b = 120, t = 60),
                       xaxis = list(title = "", tickangle = -45), yaxis = list(title = "")))
}

# Per-sample value over the cohort timepoint order: one line per patient (and compartment).
# d: patient_, timepoint, origin, val, cells (alias optional).
over_time <- function(d, title, ylab, tickformat = NULL, height = 440) {
  if (!"alias" %in% names(d)) d$alias <- ""
  d <- d %>% mutate(tp = factor(timepoint, levels = gx_tp_levels),
                    line = if (dplyr::n_distinct(origin) > 1) paste(patient_, origin, sep = " · ") else patient_) %>%
    arrange(line, tp)
  pconf(plotly::plot_ly(d, x = ~tp, y = ~val, color = ~line, colors = pal, type = "scatter",
                        mode = "lines+markers", marker = list(size = 9),
                        text = ~paste0(alias, "<br>", line, " · ", timepoint, "<br>", signif(val, 3), " (", cells, " cells)"),
                        hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>") %>%
        plotly::layout(title = ttl(title), height = height, margin = list(t = 60),
                       xaxis = list(title = "Timepoint", categoryorder = "array", categoryarray = gx_tp_levels),
                       yaxis = list(title = ylab, tickformat = tickformat),
                       legend = list(title = list(text = "Patient"))))
}

# Embedding scatter (WebGL), downsampled so the HTML stays light.
emb_plot <- function(d, colour, cols, title, max_points = 30000, hover = NULL, legend_title = "") {
  set.seed(1)
  if (nrow(d) > max_points) d <- d[sample.int(nrow(d), max_points), , drop = FALSE]
  d$.x <- d[[gx_emb[1]]]; d$.y <- d[[gx_emb[2]]]; d$.c <- factor(d[[colour]], levels = names(cols))
  d$.h <- if (is.null(hover)) paste0(d$annot, "<br>", d$alias, "<br>", d$size_bin) else hover(d)
  d <- d[order(d$.c != "no TCR", d$clone_size, na.last = FALSE), , drop = FALSE]
  pconf(plotly::plot_ly(d, x = ~.x, y = ~.y, color = ~.c, colors = cols,
                        type = "scattergl", mode = "markers", marker = list(size = 3),
                        text = ~.h, hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>") %>%
        plotly::layout(title = ttl(title), height = 560, margin = list(t = 60),
                       xaxis = list(title = "UMAP 1", showticklabels = FALSE, zeroline = FALSE, showgrid = FALSE),
                       yaxis = list(title = "UMAP 2", showticklabels = FALSE, zeroline = FALSE, showgrid = FALSE),
                       legend = list(itemsizing = "constant", title = list(text = legend_title))))
}
```

## Overview {#sec-sc-gex-overview}

```{r}
#| label: gex-overview
if (have(gx)) {
  ov_gex <- data.frame(
    Metric = c("Cells in the GEX object", "Cells with a productive TCR", "TCR+ fraction",
               "Cells with paired alpha/beta", "Cells in expanded clones (>= 2 cells)",
               "Distinct clonotypes", "Cell states", "Samples",
               if (!is.null(gx_cond)) "Conditions"),
    Value = c(format(nrow(gx), big.mark = ","), format(sum(gx$has_tcr), big.mark = ","),
              percent(mean(gx$has_tcr), 0.1),
              if ("paired_tcr" %in% names(gx)) format(sum(toupper(gx$paired_tcr) %in% c("TRUE", "T", "1")), big.mark = ",") else NA,
              format(sum(gx$expanded), big.mark = ","),
              format(dplyr::n_distinct(gx_tcr$clone_id), big.mark = ","),
              as.character(dplyr::n_distinct(gx$annot)), as.character(n_distinct_real(gx$sample)),
              if (!is.null(gx_cond)) paste(sort(unique(gx[[gx_cond]])), collapse = ", ")),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  save_table(ov_gex, "gex_overview.tsv")
  withcap(itable(ov_gex, pageSize = 10), "GEX overview",
          paste("Size of the joined dataset. The TCR+ fraction is the share of GEX cells that received a",
                "receptor; in tumour or tissue samples it is usually 50-90% (lower if non-T cells were kept).",
                "Cells in expanded clones are counted within their own sample."), kind = "Table")
}
```


## The cell-state map {#sec-sc-gex-map}

The GEX embedding (UMAP) places transcriptionally similar cells together. The first map shows
the cell states; the second colours each cell by the size of its clone in its sample, so the
two together show which programmes the expansion feeds.

```{r}
#| label: gex-umap-state
if (have(gx)) {
  if (is.null(gx_emb)) note("No embedding coordinates in the export; the cell-state map cannot be drawn.") else
    withcap(emb_plot(gx, "annot", state_cols(gx$annot), "Cells coloured by cell state", legend_title = "Cell state"),
            "Cell states on the UMAP",
            paste("Each dot is one cell (up to 30,000 shown), coloured by its annotation from the GEX object.",
                  "Click a state in the legend to hide it, double-click to show it alone. Distances between",
                  "clusters on a UMAP are only roughly meaningful: neighbouring states are similar, distant",
                  "ones not necessarily very different."))
}
```


```{r}
#| label: gex-umap-size
if (have(gx) && !is.null(gx_emb)) {
  withcap(emb_plot(gx, "size_bin", setNames(size_cols, size_levels),
                   "Cells coloured by the size of their clone in the sample",
                   hover = function(d) paste0(d$annot, "<br>", d$alias, "<br>clone size ", d$clone_size),
                   legend_title = "Clone size in sample"),
          "Clone size on the UMAP",
          paste("The same cells coloured by how many cells of their clone are in the same sample: grey",
                "singletons, blues small to large expansions, red clones of more than 20 cells; light grey",
                "cells have no receptor. Expanded clones (blue to red) that gather in one region share a",
                "transcriptional programme; clones scattered across the map span several states."))
}
```


## Cell-state composition {#sec-sc-gex-composition}

The share of each state per sample (and per condition, when the export carries one). Shifts
between samples, for example from naive or memory towards effector or exhausted states, show
the T-cell compartment being remodelled.

```{r}
#| label: gex-composition-sample
if (have(gx)) {
  d <- gx %>% count(alias, annot, name = "n") %>% group_by(alias) %>%
    mutate(val = n / sum(n)) %>% ungroup() %>%
    transmute(cat = factor(alias, levels = rev(gx_alias_levels)), grp = annot, val,
              hover = paste0(alias, "<br>", annot, ": ", percent(val, 0.1), " (", n, " cells)"))
  save_table(d %>% select(sample = cat, annot = grp, fraction = val), "gex_state_composition_by_sample.tsv")
  withcap(sbar(d, "Cell-state composition per sample", "Fraction of cells",
               height = max(420, 26 * dplyr::n_distinct(d$cat) + 160), colors = state_cols(gx$annot), legend_title = "Cell state"),
          "Cell-state composition per sample",
          paste("One bar per sample (all cells, with or without a receptor), ordered by patient and then",
                "timepoint from the top; segments are the share of each state. Read a patient's bars from",
                "top to bottom to follow its compartment over time. Samples with few cells give noisy",
                "fractions: hover a segment for the cell count."))
}
```


```{r}
#| label: gex-composition-condition
if (have(gx) && !is.null(gx_cond)) {
  # One value per sample, so samples with many cells do not dominate the comparison.
  d <- gx %>% count(sample, alias, cond = .data[[gx_cond]], annot, name = "n") %>%
    group_by(sample) %>% mutate(frac = n / sum(n)) %>% ungroup() %>%
    tidyr::complete(tidyr::nesting(sample, alias, cond), annot, fill = list(n = 0, frac = 0))
  save_table(d, "gex_state_fraction_by_sample_condition.tsv")
  withcap(pconf(plotly::plot_ly(d, x = ~annot, y = ~frac, color = ~cond, colors = pal, type = "box",
                                boxpoints = "all", jitter = 0.3, pointpos = 0,
                                text = ~paste0(alias, "<br>", annot, ": ", percent(frac, 0.1)),
                                hoverinfo = "text") %>%
                plotly::layout(boxmode = "group", title = ttl("Cell-state fractions per sample, by condition"),
                               height = 480, margin = list(t = 60, b = 110),
                               xaxis = list(title = "", tickangle = -30),
                               yaxis = list(title = "Fraction of the sample's cells", tickformat = ".0%"),
                               legend = list(orientation = "h", y = -0.3, title = list(text = "Condition")))),
          "Cell-state fractions by condition",
          paste("Each point is one sample's share of that state, boxes grouped by condition (legend).",
                "Because every sample counts once, a difference between boxes is not driven by the",
                "samples with the most cells."))
}
```


## Which cell states carry the clonal expansion {#sec-sc-gex-expansion}

**Why it matters.** Expansion concentrated in effector or exhausted states is the usual
footprint of an ongoing antigen-driven response; naive cells should stay unexpanded.

**How to read it.** The heatmap gives, for each sample (column, grouped by patient and ordered
by timepoint) and state (row), the share of TCR+ cells in expanded clones; groups with fewer
than 10 TCR+ cells are blank and vertical lines separate patients. Look for states whose
expansion grows or shrinks across a patient's timepoints. The stacked bars below then give each
state's clone-size distribution over all samples.

```{r}
#| label: gex-expansion-heatmap
if (have(gx_tcr) && dplyr::n_distinct(gx_tcr$annot) > 1) {
  top <- names(sort(table(gx_tcr$annot), decreasing = TRUE))[seq_len(min(20, dplyr::n_distinct(gx_tcr$annot)))]
  d <- gx_tcr %>% filter(annot %in% top) %>% group_by(sample, annot) %>%
    summarise(cells = n(), frac = mean(expanded), .groups = "drop") %>% filter(cells >= 10)
  if (!nrow(d)) note("No sample x cell-state group reaches 10 TCR+ cells.") else {
    so <- gx_samples %>% filter(sample %in% d$sample)
    so$lab <- so$alias
    rows <- d %>% group_by(annot) %>% summarise(m = mean(frac), .groups = "drop") %>% arrange(desc(m)) %>% pull(annot)
    m <- matrix(NA_real_, length(rows), nrow(so), dimnames = list(rows, so$lab))
    h <- matrix("", length(rows), nrow(so), dimnames = list(rows, so$lab))
    idx <- cbind(match(d$annot, rows), match(d$sample, so$sample))
    m[idx] <- d$frac
    h[idx] <- paste0(d$annot, "<br>", so$lab[idx[, 2]], " (", so$patient_[idx[, 2]], ", ",
                     so$timepoint[idx[, 2]], ")<br>", percent(d$frac, 0.1), " of ", d$cells,
                     " TCR+ cells in expanded clones")
    save_table(d %>% mutate(alias = so$lab[match(sample, so$sample)]), "gex_expanded_fraction_by_sample_state_heatmap.tsv")
    br <- which(so$patient_[-1] != so$patient_[-nrow(so)])
    withcap(pconf(plotly::plot_ly(x = so$lab, y = rows, z = m, type = "heatmap", colorscale = "YlOrRd",
                                  zmin = 0, zmax = 1, text = h, hoverinfo = "text",
                                  colorbar = list(title = "Expanded", tickformat = ".0%")) %>%
                    plotly::layout(title = ttl("Fraction of TCR+ cells in expanded clones, per sample and cell state"),
                                   height = max(420, 26 * length(rows) + 200), margin = list(l = 160, b = 120, t = 60),
                                   xaxis = list(title = "Sample (by patient, then timepoint)", tickangle = -45,
                                                categoryorder = "array", categoryarray = so$lab),
                                   yaxis = list(title = "", autorange = "reversed"),
                                   shapes = lapply(br, function(i) list(type = "line", xref = "x", yref = "paper",
                                                                        x0 = i - 0.5, x1 = i - 0.5, y0 = 0, y1 = 1,
                                                                        line = list(color = "black", width = 1))))),
            "Expansion by sample and cell state",
            paste("Colour is the share of a state's TCR+ cells, in one sample, that belong to a clone with at",
                  "least 2 cells in that sample (pale = mostly singletons, dark red = mostly expanded). States",
                  "are ordered by their mean expansion, most expanded at the top; blank tiles have fewer than",
                  "10 TCR+ cells. Small samples look less expanded simply because fewer cells were captured,",
                  "so compare a state across samples of similar size."))
  }
}
```

### Clone-size distribution per cell state {#sec-sc-gex-clone-size}

The same expansion, pooled over samples and split by clone size. It can be counted two ways,
which answer different questions:

- **By cells** (first tab): of all TCR+ cells in a state, what share sits in clones of each
  size. This is what a cell sampled at random from that state looks like: in an expanded state
  most of its cells belong to big clones, even if those clones are few.
- **By clones** (second tab): of all clones present in a state, what share has each size. A
  clone counts once, however many cells it has, so the plot shows how many distinct clones
  expanded rather than how many cells they produced. A clone with cells in several states counts
  once in each of them.

A state can look highly expanded by cells but not by clones: then one or a few very large
clones dominate it. When both views agree, many different clones expanded in that state.

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### By cells

```{r}
#| label: gex-expansion-state
if (have(gx_tcr)) {
  d <- gx_tcr %>% count(annot, size_bin, name = "n") %>% group_by(annot) %>%
    mutate(val = n / sum(n)) %>% ungroup() %>%
    mutate(grp = factor(size_bin, levels = size_levels[1:5])) %>%
    transmute(cat = annot, grp, val,
              hover = paste0(annot, "<br>", size_bin, ": ", percent(val, 0.1), " of TCR+ cells (", n, " cells)"))
  save_table(d %>% select(annot = cat, size_bin = grp, fraction = val), "gex_clone_size_by_state.tsv")
  withcap(pconf(plotly::plot_ly(d, x = ~val, y = ~cat, color = ~grp, colors = size_cols[1:5],
                                type = "bar", orientation = "h",
                                text = ~hover, hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>") %>%
                plotly::layout(barmode = "stack", title = ttl("Clone-size distribution of TCR+ cells per cell state"),
                               height = max(420, 30 * dplyr::n_distinct(d$cat) + 160), margin = list(l = 140, t = 60),
                               xaxis = list(title = "Fraction of the state's TCR+ cells", tickformat = ".0%"),
                               yaxis = list(title = ""),
                               legend = list(orientation = "h", y = -0.15, title = list(text = "Clone size in sample")))),
          "Clone size by cells",
          paste("Each bar is one state and sums to 100% of its TCR+ cells; a segment is the share of those",
                "cells whose clone has that many cells in the same sample. Example: a 40% red segment means",
                "40% of the state's cells belong to clones of more than 20 cells. A long grey segment",
                "(singletons) marks a state of mostly unexpanded, diverse cells, as expected for naive cells."))
}
```

#### By clones

```{r}
#| label: gex-expansion-state-clones
if (have(gx_tcr)) {
  d <- gx_tcr %>% distinct(sample, clone_id, annot, size_bin) %>% count(annot, size_bin, name = "n") %>%
    group_by(annot) %>% mutate(val = n / sum(n)) %>% ungroup() %>%
    mutate(grp = factor(size_bin, levels = size_levels[1:5])) %>%
    transmute(cat = annot, grp, val,
              hover = paste0(annot, "<br>", size_bin, ": ", percent(val, 0.1), " of clones (", n, " clones)"))
  save_table(d %>% select(annot = cat, size_bin = grp, fraction = val), "gex_clone_size_by_state_clones.tsv")
  withcap(pconf(plotly::plot_ly(d, x = ~val, y = ~cat, color = ~grp, colors = size_cols[1:5],
                                type = "bar", orientation = "h",
                                text = ~hover, hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>") %>%
                plotly::layout(barmode = "stack", title = ttl("Clone-size distribution of clones per cell state"),
                               height = max(420, 30 * dplyr::n_distinct(d$cat) + 160), margin = list(l = 140, t = 60),
                               xaxis = list(title = "Fraction of the state's clones", tickformat = ".0%"),
                               yaxis = list(title = ""),
                               legend = list(orientation = "h", y = -0.15, title = list(text = "Clone size in sample")))),
          "Clone size by clones",
          paste("Each bar sums to 100% of the clones with at least one cell in the state; a segment is the",
                "share of those clones with that size. Within a bar a clone counts once per sample (once in",
                "each sample it was found in), however many of its cells are in the state. A clone with cells in",
                "several states counts once in each of those bars, so the bars are not exclusive and their",
                "counts do not add up to the number of clones. Size is the clone's cells in the whole sample,",
                "not only in that state. Most clones are singletons in almost every state, so look at how far",
                "the coloured segments reach rather than at the grey."))
}
```

## Cell states of clones that expand or contract over time {#sec-sc-gex-dynamics}

**What it shows.** Clones called *expanding* or *contracting* by the clonal dynamics analysis (a
significant frequency change between two timepoints of the same patient and compartment;
Fisher's exact test, FDR < 0.05), traced back to their cells across all of the patient's
samples. *Other expanded* are clones of ≥ 2 cells in a sample whose change did not reach
significance, mostly in patients with a single timepoint.

**Why it matters.** It tells whether the clones the treatment or disease course selects for
have a distinct phenotype.

**How to read it.** One panel per patient. A response typically shows expanding clones enriched
for effector/cytotoxic or exhausted states and contracting clones drifting towards memory or
naive states.

```{r}
#| label: gex-dynamics-states
cd_exp <- T("clonal", "expanded_clones_summary.csv")
cd_con <- T("clonal", "contracting_clones_summary.csv")
if (!have(gx_tcr)) {
  invisible(NULL)
} else if (!have(cd_exp) && !have(cd_con)) {
  note(paste("No clone expanded or contracted significantly between two timepoints of the same patient",
             "and compartment: either no patient was sampled twice in a compartment, or no change passed the test."))
} else {
  pick <- function(t, lab) {
    if (!have(t)) return(NULL)
    pc <- intersect(c(as_str1(params$patient_col), "patient", "patient_id", "subject_id"), names(t))[1]
    if (is.na(pc) || !"junction_aa" %in% names(t)) return(NULL)
    data.frame(patient_ = as.character(t[[pc]]), cdr3b = as.character(t$junction_aa), status = lab) %>% distinct()
  }
  cd_status <- bind_rows(pick(cd_exp, "Expanding"), pick(cd_con, "Contracting")) %>%
    group_by(patient_, cdr3b) %>%
    summarise(status = if (dplyr::n_distinct(status) == 1) first(status) else "Both", .groups = "drop")
  cc <- gx_tcr %>% left_join(cd_status, by = c("patient_", "cdr3b")) %>%
    mutate(status = coalesce(status, ifelse(expanded, "Other expanded", "Not expanded")))
  top <- names(sort(table(gx_tcr$annot), decreasing = TRUE))[seq_len(min(12, dplyr::n_distinct(gx_tcr$annot)))]
  cc$annot2 <- ifelse(cc$annot %in% top, cc$annot, "Other")
  lv <- intersect(c("Expanding", "Contracting", "Both", "Other expanded", "Not expanded"), unique(cc$status))
  d <- cc %>% count(patient_, status, annot2, name = "n") %>% group_by(patient_, status) %>%
    mutate(frac = n / sum(n)) %>% ungroup() %>% mutate(status = factor(status, levels = lv))
  save_table(d, "gex_dynamics_state_composition.tsv")
  cols <- state_cols(d$annot2)
  pats <- sort(unique(d$patient_))
  plots <- lapply(seq_along(pats), function(k) {
    dd <- d %>% filter(patient_ == pats[k])
    plotly::plot_ly(dd, x = ~status, y = ~frac, color = ~annot2, colors = cols, type = "bar",
                    legendgroup = ~annot2, showlegend = k == 1,
                    text = ~paste0(pats[k], "<br>", status, "<br>", annot2, ": ", percent(frac, 0.1), " (", n, " cells)"),
                    hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>") %>%
      plotly::layout(barmode = "stack",
                     annotations = list(list(text = pats[k], x = 0.5, y = 1.06, xref = "paper", yref = "paper",
                                             showarrow = FALSE, font = list(size = 13))))
  })
  nr <- ceiling(length(plots) / 4)
  withcap(pconf(plotly::subplot(plots, nrows = nr, shareY = TRUE, margin = 0.04) %>%
                plotly::layout(barmode = "stack", title = ttl("Cell states of significantly expanding and contracting clones"),
                               height = 380 * nr + 80, margin = list(t = 80),
                               yaxis = list(title = "Fraction of cells", tickformat = ".0%"),
                               legend = list(title = list(text = "Cell state")))),
          "Cell states by clonal dynamics",
          paste("One panel per patient; each bar is a group of clones and sums to 100% of their cells, across",
                "all of the patient's samples. <em>Expanding</em>/<em>Contracting</em>: significant change between",
                "two timepoints; <em>Both</em>: expanding in one comparison and contracting in another;",
                "<em>Other expanded</em>: ≥ 2 cells in a sample, no significant change; <em>Not expanded</em>:",
                "singletons. Compare the Expanding bar with Not expanded: states enriched in the first are",
                "the phenotype of the responding clones. Bars of few clones (hover for cell counts) are noisy."))
}
```

## Clones shared between cell states {#sec-sc-gex-sharing}

**What it shows.** How often an expanded clone has cells in two different states at once.

**Why it matters.** The cells of one clone all derive from one naive T cell, so a clone found
in two states shows a differentiation path between them (for example effector to exhausted, or
memory to effector). States that share many clones are developmentally linked; states that
share none are separate lineages (for example CD4 Treg and CD8 effector).

**How to read it.** In the heatmap, each tile counts the expanded clones with cells in both the
row and the column state *in the same sample*, counted once per patient; hover a tile for its
breakdown by patient. The diagonal counts the expanded clones with any cell in that state. The
table lists the off-diagonal pairs, most shared first, with one column per patient and the
breakdown by sample.

```{r}
#| label: gex-state-sharing
if (have(gx_tcr) && dplyr::n_distinct(gx_tcr$annot) > 1) {
  # A clone is counted per sample, so the same receptor in two patients is not a shared clone;
  # a clone shared in several samples of a patient counts once for that patient.
  occ <- gx_tcr %>% filter(expanded) %>% distinct(patient_, sample, clone_id, annot)
  if (!nrow(occ)) note("No expanded clones to compare across cell states.") else {
    st <- sort(unique(gx_tcr$annot))
    pairs <- occ %>% inner_join(occ, by = c("patient_", "sample", "clone_id"), relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
      distinct(patient_, clone_id, annot.x, annot.y)
    tab <- pairs %>% count(annot.x, annot.y, name = "n")
    by_pat <- pairs %>% count(annot.x, annot.y, patient_, name = "n") %>% arrange(patient_) %>%
      group_by(annot.x, annot.y) %>%
      summarise(breakdown = paste0(patient_, ": ", n, collapse = "<br>"), .groups = "drop")
    m <- matrix(0, length(st), length(st), dimnames = list(st, st))
    h <- matrix("", length(st), length(st), dimnames = list(st, st))
    m[cbind(tab$annot.x, tab$annot.y)] <- tab$n
    h[] <- paste0(rep(st, times = length(st)), " / ", rep(st, each = length(st)), "<br>0 clones")
    tb <- tab %>% left_join(by_pat, by = c("annot.x", "annot.y"))
    h[cbind(tb$annot.x, tb$annot.y)] <- paste0(tb$annot.x, " / ", tb$annot.y, "<br><b>", tb$n, " clones</b><br>", tb$breakdown)
    save_table(as.data.frame(m) %>% tibble::rownames_to_column("annot"), "gex_state_clone_sharing.tsv")
    # The diagonal (all expanded clones of a state) dwarfs the shared counts, so the colour
    # scale runs up to the largest off-diagonal value and the diagonal saturates.
    off <- m; diag(off) <- 0
    zmax <- if (max(off) > 0) max(off) else max(m)
    withcap(hmap(m, "Expanded clones found in both cell states", "Clones",
                 colorscale = list(list(0, "#e6e6e6"), list(0.5, "#6baed6"), list(1, "#08306b")),
                 text = h, zmin = 0, zmax = zmax, height = max(480, 28 * length(st) + 220)),
            "Clones shared between cell states",
            paste("Each tile is the number of expanded clones with cells in both states in the same sample",
                  "(grey = none, dark blue = most). The colour scale stops at the largest shared count, so",
                  "diagonal tiles (all expanded clones of a state) are drawn at the darkest blue; hover any tile",
                  "for the exact count and its split by patient. A pair shared in only one patient may reflect",
                  "one dominant clone rather than a general path."))
  }
}
```

```{r}
#| label: gex-state-sharing-table
if (exists("pairs") && is.data.frame(pairs) && nrow(pairs)) {
  d <- pairs %>% filter(annot.x < annot.y) %>% count(state_a = annot.x, state_b = annot.y, patient_, name = "n") %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = patient_, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
  pcols <- setdiff(names(d), c("state_a", "state_b"))
  d$clones <- rowSums(d[, pcols, drop = FALSE])
  d$patients <- rowSums(d[, pcols, drop = FALSE] > 0)
  # Per-sample breakdown: expanded clones with cells in both states within that sample.
  by_sample <- occ %>% inner_join(occ, by = c("patient_", "sample", "clone_id"), relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
    filter(annot.x < annot.y) %>% distinct(patient_, sample, clone_id, annot.x, annot.y) %>%
    count(state_a = annot.x, state_b = annot.y, patient_, sample, name = "n") %>%
    left_join(gx_tcr %>% distinct(sample, alias, timepoint, origin), by = "sample") %>%
    mutate(.tp = match(timepoint, gx_tp_levels)) %>%
    arrange(patient_, origin, .tp, alias) %>%
    group_by(state_a, state_b) %>%
    summarise(samples = paste0(alias, " (", n, ")", collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop")
  d <- d[, c("state_a", "state_b", "clones", "patients", sort(pcols))] %>%
    left_join(by_sample, by = c("state_a", "state_b")) %>% arrange(desc(clones))
  save_table(d, "gex_state_clone_sharing_pairs.tsv")
  if (nrow(d)) withcap(itable(as.data.frame(d), pageSize = 10), "State pairs sharing expanded clones",
                       paste("One row per pair of states, with the number of shared expanded clones in total, the",
                             "number of patients in which the pair is shared, the count per patient, and in",
                             "<code>samples</code> the count per sample (alias, in timepoint order). A clone counts",
                             "once per patient in the patient columns but once in every sample where it has cells in",
                             "both states, so the sample counts can add up to more than the patient count; a pair",
                             "found in several samples of a patient is a stable link rather than a one-off. Pairs",
                             "shared across several patients are the most general differentiation links."),
                       kind = "Table")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: gex-plasticity
if (have(gx_tcr)) {
  d <- gx_tcr %>% filter(expanded) %>% group_by(patient = patient_, sample = alias, clone_id) %>%
    summarise(cdr3b = first(cdr3b), cells = n(), states = dplyr::n_distinct(annot),
              main_state = names(which.max(table(annot))),
              main_frac = max(table(annot)) / n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(desc(cells)) %>% select(-clone_id)
  save_table(d, "gex_clone_state_plasticity.tsv")
  withcap(itable(head(d, 200) %>% mutate(main_frac = round(main_frac, 3)), pageSize = 10),
          "Cell states of the largest expanded clones",
          paste("The 200 largest expanded clones (per sample), with the number of states their cells occupy,",
                "the dominant state and the share of the clone's cells in it. <code>main_frac</code> near 1",
                "means a phenotypically committed clone; low values with several states mean a clone whose",
                "cells are spread over a differentiation path."), kind = "Table")
}
```

## Gene expression of cell states and expanded cells {#sec-sc-gex-genes}

Canonical T-cell genes (naive/memory, cytotoxic, tissue-residency, exhaustion, MAIT,
proliferation) per state, to check the annotation, and the difference between expanded and
singleton cells within each state, to see what expansion adds beyond the state itself.

```{r}
#| label: gex-genes
gx_expr <- NULL
.rds <- as_str1(params$seurat_rds)
if (have(gx) && nzchar(.rds) && file.exists(.rds) && file.size(.rds) > 0) {
  gx_expr <- tryCatch({
    suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(Seurat))
    seu <- readRDS(.rds)
    genes <- c("CD8A", "CD8B", "CD4", "SELL", "CCR7", "TCF7", "IL7R", "GZMK", "GZMA", "GZMB",
               "PRF1", "GNLY", "NKG7", "IFNG", "CX3CR1", "KLRG1", "ITGAE", "CD69", "ZNF683",
               "PDCD1", "HAVCR2", "LAG3", "TIGIT", "CTLA4", "TOX", "CXCL13", "ENTPD1",
               "KLRB1", "SLC4A10", "ZBTB16", "MKI67", "TOP2A", "FOXP3", "TRDC")
    genes <- intersect(genes, rownames(seu))
    cells <- intersect(gx$cell_id, colnames(seu))
    if (length(genes) < 2 || length(cells) < 50) NULL else {
      get_layer <- function(l) tryCatch(SeuratObject::LayerData(seu, layer = l),
                                        error = function(e) tryCatch(Seurat::GetAssayData(seu, slot = l),
                                                                     error = function(e) NULL))
      dat <- suppressWarnings(get_layer("data"))
      if (!is.null(dat) && all(dim(dat) > 0)) {
        mat <- dat[genes, cells, drop = FALSE]
      } else {
        # Downstream objects can carry counts only: LogNormalize the panel genes against
        # each cell's full library size, as Seurat's NormalizeData would.
        cnt <- get_layer("counts")[, cells, drop = FALSE]
        mat <- log1p(Matrix::t(Matrix::t(cnt[genes, , drop = FALSE]) / Matrix::colSums(cnt)) * 1e4)
      }
      rm(seu); invisible(gc())
      list(mat = as.matrix(mat), meta = gx[match(cells, gx$cell_id), , drop = FALSE])
    }
  }, error = function(e) { message("GEX expression unavailable: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })
}
if (have(gx) && is.null(gx_expr)) note("The GEX object could not be read, or shares too few cells / marker genes with the export; expression panels are skipped.")
```


```{r}
#| label: gex-markers-state
if (!is.null(gx_expr)) {
  g <- gx_expr$meta$annot
  avg <- sapply(split(seq_along(g), g), function(i) Matrix::rowMeans(gx_expr$mat[, i, drop = FALSE]))
  z <- t(scale(t(avg)))
  z[is.na(z)] <- 0
  save_table(as.data.frame(avg) %>% tibble::rownames_to_column("gene"), "gex_marker_mean_by_state.tsv")
  withcap(hmap(t(z), "Canonical T-cell genes by cell state (row-scaled mean expression)", "z-score",
               colorscale = "RdBu", zmid = 0, height = max(420, 32 * ncol(z) + 200)),
          "Marker genes by cell state",
          paste("Mean log-expression of each gene in each state, scaled per gene across states (red = highest",
                "in that state, blue = lowest). Use it to check the annotation: naive/memory states should be",
                "red for <em>SELL</em>, <em>CCR7</em>, <em>TCF7</em>, <em>IL7R</em>; cytotoxic effectors for",
                "<em>GZMB</em>, <em>PRF1</em>, <em>NKG7</em>; exhausted cells for <em>PDCD1</em>,",
                "<em>HAVCR2</em>, <em>TOX</em>, <em>CXCL13</em>; MAIT for <em>KLRB1</em>, <em>SLC4A10</em>;",
                "Treg for <em>FOXP3</em>; cycling cells for <em>MKI67</em>, <em>TOP2A</em>. Because each gene is",
                "scaled on its own, the colours compare states, not genes."))
}
```


```{r}
#| label: gex-markers-expanded
if (!is.null(gx_expr)) {
  md <- gx_expr$meta
  ok <- md$has_tcr
  # Count both groups over the same states (a state may have only one kind of cell).
  lv <- sort(unique(as.character(md$annot[ok])))
  n_exp <- table(factor(md$annot[ok & md$expanded %in% TRUE], levels = lv))
  n_sgl <- table(factor(md$annot[ok & md$expanded %in% FALSE], levels = lv))
  st <- lv[n_exp >= 20 & n_sgl >= 20]
  if (!length(st)) note("Too few expanded and non-expanded cells per state to compare expression.") else {
    lfc <- sapply(st, function(s) {
      e <- ok & md$annot == s
      Matrix::rowMeans(gx_expr$mat[, e & md$expanded, drop = FALSE]) -
        Matrix::rowMeans(gx_expr$mat[, e & !md$expanded, drop = FALSE])
    })
    save_table(as.data.frame(lfc) %>% tibble::rownames_to_column("gene"), "gex_expanded_vs_singleton_by_state.tsv")
    withcap(hmap(t(lfc), "Expanded vs singleton cells within each state (difference in mean log-expression)",
                 "Δ log-expr", colorscale = "RdBu", zmid = 0, height = max(420, 32 * length(st) + 200)),
            "Expanded vs singleton cells within each state",
            paste("Difference in mean log-expression between cells of expanded clones and singletons of the",
                  "<em>same</em> state (red = higher in expanded cells). This separates expansion-associated",
                  "programmes (for example more cytotoxicity or exhaustion in expanded clones) from differences",
                  "between states. A difference of 0.5 is about a 1.6-fold change. States need at least 20",
                  "cells of each kind; the differences are descriptive, not tested."))
  }
}
```

## CoNGA: clones with matching TCR and transcriptional neighbourhoods {#sec-sc-gex-conga}

**What it is.** CoNGA (clonotype neighbour graph analysis; Schattgen *et al.*, *Nat Biotechnol*
2022, [doi:10.1038/s41587-021-00989-2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-021-00989-2)) builds two
neighbour graphs over clonotypes, one from gene expression and one from receptor similarity
(TCRdist). A clonotype whose expression neighbours are also its receptor neighbours more often
than chance is a **CoNGA hit**: its score (a Bonferroni-adjusted p-value) is below 1, lower being
stronger. CoNGA runs once on the whole cohort, and its hit clusters (pairs of GEX and TCR
clusters) are one of the methods of the consensus clustering.

**Why it matters.** Hits are groups of similar receptors that drive a shared transcriptional
programme, the joint signal expected from T cells recognising related antigens, or from
innate-like T cells with a fixed receptor.

**How to read it.** The table summarises the run; then the share of each state's TCR+ cells that
are hits, the hits on the cell-state map, the share of hits in each sample over time (a rising
share means more of the repertoire sits in receptor groups with coherent states), and the
strongest hit clonotypes with where they were found. Invariant MAIT and iNKT receptors are
frequent hits in innate-like states and are usually not antigen-specific.

```{r}
#| label: conga
if (!have(conga_roll) && !have(conga_clusters)) {
  note("CoNGA produced no output on this run.")
} else {
  if (have(conga_roll)) save_table(conga_roll, "master_conga_rollup.tsv")
  if (have(conga_clusters)) save_table(conga_clusters, "master_conga_clusters.tsv")
  withcap(itable(if (have(conga_roll)) conga_roll else conga_clusters, pageSize = 15), "CoNGA run summary",
          paste("Cells and clonotypes CoNGA scored, and how many reached a hit. Few or no hits is common in",
                "small cohorts or when most clones are singletons, and does not mean the run failed."),
          kind = "Table")
}
```


```{r}
#| label: gex-conga-state
if (have(gx_tcr) && "conga_score" %in% names(gx_tcr) && any(!is.na(gx_tcr$conga_score))) {
  # CoNGA score is a Bonferroni-adjusted p-value: < 1 marks a GEX/TCR neighbourhood hit.
  gx_tcr$conga_hit <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(gx_tcr$conga_score)) < 1
  d <- gx_tcr %>% filter(!is.na(conga_hit)) %>% group_by(annot) %>%
    summarise(cells = n(), hits = sum(conga_hit), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(val = hits / cells)
  save_table(d, "gex_conga_hits_by_state.tsv")
  withcap(hbar(d %>% transmute(cat = annot, val, hover = paste0(annot, "<br>", hits, " / ", cells, " TCR+ cells (",
                                                                percent(val, 0.1), ")")),
               "CoNGA hits by cell state", "Fraction of TCR+ cells that are CoNGA hits",
               tickformat = ".0%", height = max(400, 30 * nrow(d) + 140)),
          "CoNGA hits by cell state",
          paste("Share of each state's TCR+ cells whose clonotype is a CoNGA hit. States at the top hold",
                "receptor groups with a coherent expression programme: MAIT or iNKT at the top reflect their",
                "invariant receptors, while effector or exhausted states at the top are the candidate",
                "antigen-driven signal."))
} else if (have(gx_tcr)) note("No per-cell CoNGA scores were exported.")
```

```{r}
  sc <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(gx$conga_score))
  gx$conga_lab <- ifelse(!is.na(sc) & sc < 1, "CoNGA hit", ifelse(gx$has_tcr, "TCR+, not a hit", "no TCR"))
  withcap(emb_plot(gx, "conga_lab", c("CoNGA hit" = "#de2d26", "TCR+, not a hit" = "#9ecae1", "no TCR" = "#ececec"),
                   "CoNGA hits on the cell-state map",
                   hover = function(d) paste0(d$annot, "<br>", d$alias, "<br>", d$conga_lab, "<br>clone size ", d$clone_size),
                   legend_title = "CoNGA"),
          "CoNGA hits on the UMAP",
          paste("Red cells belong to hit clonotypes. Hits forming a compact patch in one region are a receptor",
                "group with one shared programme; compare the patch with the cell-state map above."))
}
```

```{r}
  d <- gx_tcr %>% filter(!is.na(conga_hit)) %>% group_by(sample, alias, patient_, timepoint, origin) %>%
    summarise(cells = n(), val = mean(conga_hit), .groups = "drop")
  withcap(over_time(d, "Share of TCR+ cells in CoNGA hit clonotypes over time", "CoNGA hits", tickformat = ".0%"),
          "CoNGA hits over time",
          paste("One line per patient (and compartment), one point per sample at its timepoint: the share of",
                "the sample's TCR+ cells whose clonotype is a CoNGA hit (score < 1). Timepoints a patient was not",
                "sampled at are skipped, not drawn as 0. See the box below for how to read the trend."))
}
```

:::: {.callout-note title="Reading the CoNGA trend over time" collapse="false"}
CoNGA scores every clonotype once, on the whole cohort, so a clone's score does not change between
timepoints. What changes is **how many of each sample's T cells belong to hit clonotypes**, and
that is what the lines follow.

- **Rising.** A growing share of the repertoire sits in receptor groups that share one
  transcriptional programme. Usually hit clones expanded (or new clones of a hit group arrived),
  as in an antigen-driven response that is focusing: similar receptors recruited into one
  effector or exhausted state. Check which states the hits sit in (CoNGA hits by cell state) and
  which clones drive it (the table below) before calling it tumour-specific: MAIT/iNKT hits rising
  reflect innate-like cells, not an antigen response.
- **Falling.** Hit clones contracted or were diluted by many new, unrelated clones: the response
  that linked receptor to phenotype is receding, or the repertoire is diversifying (for example
  after lymphodepletion recovery). In tissue it can also mean the hit clones left the site.
- **Stable.** The receptor–phenotype coupling is maintained: either persistent hit clones at
  a steady share (a sustained, stable programme) or a low baseline with no structured response.
  The level matters: stable at 20% and stable at 1% mean different things.

Shares are noisy for samples with few TCR+ cells (hover for the cell count), and a single large
hit clone can move a line on its own, so confirm a trend with the hit clonotype table.
::::

```{r}
#| label: gex-conga-top
if (have(gx_tcr) && any(gx_tcr$conga_hit %in% TRUE)) {
  d <- gx_tcr %>% filter(conga_hit %in% TRUE) %>% group_by(patient = patient_, clone_id) %>%
    summarise(cdr3b = first(cdr3b), cells = n(), best_score = min(as.numeric(conga_score)),
              state = names(which.max(table(annot))),
              timepoints = paste(intersect(gx_tp_levels, unique(timepoint)), collapse = ", "),
              compartments = paste(sort(unique(origin)), collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(best_score, desc(cells)) %>% select(-clone_id)
  save_table(d, "gex_conga_top_hits.tsv")
  withcap(itable(d %>% mutate(best_score = signif(best_score, 3)), pageSize = 10), "CoNGA hit clonotypes",
          paste("Hit clonotypes, strongest first: the CoNGA score (lower = stronger), cells, dominant state and",
                "the timepoints and compartments the clone was found at. Hits present at several timepoints",
                "are persistent clones with a stable programme, the best candidates for follow-up."),
          kind = "Table")
}
```

## TCRi: phenotype bias encoded in the receptor {#sec-sc-gex-tcri}

**What it is.** TCRi (Ceglia *et al.*, [bioRxiv 2022.10.01.510457](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2022.10.01.510457v1);
[github.com/nceglia/tcri](https://github.com/nceglia/tcri)) is an information-theoretic
framework for paired TCR and GEX data. Its probabilistic model learns, for each clonotype, a
distribution over phenotypes from its cells' expression. A cell's **TCRi score** is the
probability of its most likely phenotype (the *predicted* phenotype); cells are grouped Low,
Mid and High by score.

**Why it matters.** It measures how strongly clonal identity determines cell fate: if a clone's
cells consistently adopt one state, the receptor (or the antigen it sees) is shaping that fate;
if not, the environment dominates.

**What high and low values mean.** The score runs from about 1 / (number of phenotypes) to 1.

- **High (close to 1)**: the model is confident about the clone's phenotype, and its cells are
  committed to one fate. This is expected for clones driven by a persistent antigen (for
  example exhausted tumour-reactive clones), and for Treg and MAIT cells, whose lineage is fixed.
- **Low (near the minimum)**: the clone's cells are spread over several phenotypes with no
  clear favourite. The clone is plastic, or its fate is set by the environment rather than by
  its receptor.
- Singleton clones carry little information, so their scores mostly reflect the cell's own
  state; the signal is in expanded clones.

**How to read it.** Scores by observed state show which states hold the most committed clones;
the time course shows whether commitment grows over a patient's samples; the tables compare,
for expanded clones, the phenotype TCRi predicts with the one observed. Agreement means a
clone-intrinsic fate bias, disagreement an environment-driven state.

::: {.callout-note title="TCRi and phenotypic plasticity" collapse="false"}
**Phenotypic plasticity** is the ability of one clone, all of whose cells carry the same
receptor, to give rise to cells in different functional states: for example effector and
memory progeny of the same clone, a progenitor-exhausted (TCF7+) pool that keeps feeding
terminally exhausted cells, or a clone found as circulating effector cells in blood and as
resident or exhausted cells in the tumour. TCRi turns this into a number: a clone's TCRi score is
high when its cells concentrate in one phenotype and low when they spread over several, so the
**score is the inverse of the clone's plasticity**.

- **Expanded, high TCRi (fate-restricted clones).** Many cells, nearly all in one state. Typical of
  chronic, persistent antigen exposure (tumour-reactive clones driven to exhaustion), of
  terminally differentiated effectors, and of lineage-fixed cells (Treg, MAIT). These clones have
  limited capacity to renew themselves or to switch programme.
- **Expanded, low TCRi (plastic clones).** Many cells spread across states. Expected in an ongoing
  or recall response, where one clone sustains effector, memory and proliferating branches at the
  same time; in tumours, a clone with both progenitor-exhausted and effector cells is the
  population that immune checkpoint blockade is thought to reinvigorate. Plastic clones are
  often the most durable part of a response.
- **Small clones.** With few cells, both a high and a low score are poorly determined: judge
  plasticity from expanded clones (the clone-level plasticity map below).

**Over time.** Within a patient, a falling mean TCRi means clones are diversifying their states
(new effector or memory branches, for example after therapy or antigen re-exposure); a rising
mean means they are converging on one state (commitment, often terminal differentiation or
exhaustion under persistent antigen). Read this together with *Cell states by clonal dynamics*
above: expanding clones that are also plastic are actively generating new effector cells, while
expanding clones that are fate-restricted are accumulating in one state.

**Predicted versus observed.** When TCRi's predicted phenotype differs from the state most of a
clone's cells were annotated as, the clone is split between states and the model weighs the
minority state more strongly from its expression: a sign of a clone in transition between
states rather than of an annotation error.

**Caveats.** Apparent plasticity depends on the annotation: finer annotations (more, smaller
states) make every clone look more plastic, and neighbouring states along a continuum (for example
effector memory and effector) can split one programme in two. Clones pooled over blood and
tissue may look plastic only because the two compartments impose different states. Doublets and
ambient contamination can add spurious states to large clones. Compare TCRi between patients
annotated in the same way, and confirm interesting clones in the per-sample views of the
**Details: Sample** report (cell-state make-up of the largest clones, phenotypic heterogeneity).
:::

```{r}
#| label: tcri
if (!have(tcri_roll)) {
  note("TCRi produced no output on this run.")
} else {
  save_table(tcri_roll, "master_tcri_rollup.tsv")
  withcap(itable(tcri_roll, pageSize = 15), "TCRi run summary",
          "Cells and clonotypes TCRi scored, the score distribution and how many cells fall in each group.",
          kind = "Table")
}
```


```{r}
#| label: gex-tcri-state
if (have(gx_tcr) && "tcri_score" %in% names(gx_tcr) && any(!is.na(gx_tcr$tcri_score))) {
  d <- gx_tcr %>% filter(!is.na(tcri_score)) %>%
    transmute(grp = annot, val = as.numeric(tcri_score),
              hover = paste0(annot, "<br>", alias, "<br>TCRi ", round(val, 3)))
  set.seed(1)
  if (nrow(d) > 20000) d <- d[sample.int(nrow(d), 20000), ]
  withcap(boxby(d, "TCRi score by cell state", "TCRi score", angle = -30),
          "TCRi score by cell state",
          paste("Each point is one TCR+ cell (up to 20,000 shown), the box its state's quartiles. States with",
                "boxes near 1 hold clones committed to that state; low or wide boxes hold clones whose cells",
                "are also found in other states."))
} else if (have(gx_tcr)) note("No per-cell TCRi scores were exported.")
```


```{r}
#| label: gex-tcri-time
if (have(gx_tcr) && "tcri_score" %in% names(gx_tcr) && any(!is.na(gx_tcr$tcri_score))) {
  d <- gx_tcr %>% filter(!is.na(tcri_score)) %>%
    group_by(sample, alias, patient_, timepoint, origin) %>%
    summarise(cells = n(), val = mean(as.numeric(tcri_score)), .groups = "drop")
  withcap(over_time(d, "Mean TCRi score of TCR+ cells over time", "Mean TCRi score"),
          "TCRi score over time",
          paste("Mean TCRi score of each sample's TCR+ cells, one line per patient. A rising line means the",
                "patient's T cells become more committed to one fate per clone over time, as expected when a",
                "persistent antigen drives clones to a terminal state such as exhaustion."))
}
```

```{r}
#| label: gex-tcri-plasticity
if (have(gx_tcr) && "tcri_score" %in% names(gx_tcr) && any(!is.na(gx_tcr$tcri_score) & gx_tcr$expanded)) {
  # One point per expanded clone and sample: its size, mean TCRi and the number of states its
  # cells occupy (each with at least 10% of the clone's cells).
  d <- gx_tcr %>% filter(expanded, !is.na(tcri_score)) %>%
    group_by(sample, alias, patient_, clone_id) %>%
    summarise(cdr3b = first(cdr3b), cells = n(), mean_tcri = mean(as.numeric(tcri_score)),
              dominant = names(which.max(table(annot))),
              dominant_frac = max(table(annot)) / n(),
              n_states = sum(table(annot) / n() >= 0.1), .groups = "drop")
  save_table(d, "gex_tcri_clone_plasticity.tsv")
  cols <- state_cols(gx_tcr$annot)
  withcap(pconf(plotly::plot_ly(d, x = ~cells, y = ~mean_tcri, color = ~dominant, colors = cols,
                                type = "scatter", mode = "markers",
                                marker = list(size = ~pmin(6 + 2 * n_states, 16), opacity = 0.75,
                                              line = list(width = 0.5, color = "white")),
                                text = ~paste0(cdr3b, "<br>", alias, "<br>", cells, " cells, ", n_states,
                                               " state(s) ≥ 10%<br>dominant: ", dominant, " (",
                                               percent(dominant_frac, 1), ")<br>mean TCRi ", round(mean_tcri, 3)),
                                hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>") %>%
                plotly::layout(title = ttl("Clone size against TCRi: committed and plastic clones"),
                               height = 500, margin = list(t = 60),
                               xaxis = list(title = "Cells in clone (sample)", type = "log"),
                               yaxis = list(title = "Mean TCRi score of the clone's cells"),
                               legend = list(title = list(text = "Dominant state")))),
          "Clone-level plasticity map",
          paste("One point per expanded clone per sample, coloured by the state most of its cells are in;",
                "larger points span more states (each holding at least 10% of the clone's cells). Upper",
                "right: large, fate-restricted clones. Lower right: large, plastic clones whose progeny",
                "occupy several states. Clones of a few cells sit on the left, where the score is noisy.",
                "Hover a point for its CDR3β, sample and state split; the table is written as",
                "<code>gex_tcri_clone_plasticity.tsv</code>."))
}
```

```{r}
#| label: gex-tcri-top
if (have(gx_tcr) && "tcri_score" %in% names(gx_tcr) && any(!is.na(gx_tcr$tcri_score) & gx_tcr$expanded)) {
  d <- gx_tcr %>% filter(expanded, !is.na(tcri_score)) %>% group_by(patient = patient_, clone_id) %>%
    summarise(cdr3b = first(cdr3b), cells = n(), mean_tcri = mean(as.numeric(tcri_score)),
              predicted = if ("tcri_predicted_phenotype" %in% names(.) && any(!is.na(tcri_predicted_phenotype)))
                names(which.max(table(tcri_predicted_phenotype))) else NA_character_,
              observed = names(which.max(table(annot))),
              timepoints = paste(intersect(gx_tp_levels, unique(timepoint)), collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(desc(mean_tcri), desc(cells)) %>% select(-clone_id)
  save_table(d, "gex_tcri_top_expanded_clones.tsv")
  withcap(itable(d %>% mutate(mean_tcri = round(mean_tcri, 3)), pageSize = 10), "TCRi of expanded clones",
          paste("Expanded clones by mean TCRi score, with the phenotype TCRi predicts and the state most of",
                "their cells were annotated as. A high score with predicted = observed is a clone committed",
                "to that state. Predicted ≠ observed: the clone's cells are split, and the majority state is",
                "not the one the model favours."), kind = "Table")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: tcri-clones
if (have(tcri_scores)) {
  save_table(tcri_scores, "master_tcri_high_clones.tsv")
  d  <- tcri_scores
  nc <- intersect(c("n_cells", "cells", "clone_size", "n"), names(d))
  cc <- intersect(c("clone_id", "CTaa", "clonotype"), names(d))
  if (!length(nc) || !length(cc)) {
    withcap(itable(d, pageSize = 10), "High-TCRi clones", "", kind = "Table")
  } else {
    dd <- data.frame(cat = as.character(d[[cc[1]]]), val = as.numeric(d[[nc[1]]]))
    dd <- head(dd[order(-dd$val), , drop = FALSE], params$top_n_clusters)
    dd$hover <- paste0(dd$cat, "<br>", dd$val, " cells")
    withcap(hbar(dd, paste0("Top ", params$top_n_clusters, " high-TCRi clones"), "Cells", height = 560),
            "Largest high-TCRi clones",
            paste("The largest clones whose cells fall in the High TCRi group, by cells. These are the big",
                  "clones most committed to one phenotype; find them in the table above for their state."))
  }
}
```

## Consensus clusters by cell state {#sec-sc-gex-consensus}

**What it shows.** The largest consensus clusters (see Consensus clustering) split by the
states of their cells.

**Why it matters.** Consensus clusters group receptors predicted to share specificity, so a
cluster concentrated in one state points to a specificity tied to that phenotype, for example
a tumour-reactive group that is mostly exhausted.

**How to read it.** One bar per cluster (cell count in brackets), segments the share of its
cells in each state. A cluster dominated by one state is a specificity with a single fate; one
spread over several states is a specificity whose cells differentiate along a path.

```{r}
#| label: gex-consensus-state
if (have(gx_tcr) && "consensus_cluster" %in% names(gx_tcr)) {
  d <- gx_tcr %>% filter(!is.na(consensus_cluster), nzchar(as.character(consensus_cluster)),
                         !as.character(consensus_cluster) %in% c("NA", "none", "None"))
  top <- d %>% count(consensus_cluster, sort = TRUE) %>% head(params$top_n_clusters)
  if (!nrow(top)) note("No cells were assigned to a consensus cluster.") else {
    d <- d %>% filter(consensus_cluster %in% top$consensus_cluster) %>%
      count(consensus_cluster, annot, name = "n") %>% group_by(consensus_cluster) %>%
      mutate(val = n / sum(n), tot = sum(n)) %>% ungroup() %>%
      transmute(cat = paste0(consensus_cluster, " (", tot, ")"), grp = annot, val, tot,
                hover = paste0("cluster ", consensus_cluster, "<br>", annot, ": ", n, " cells"))
    # Largest cluster at the top.
    d$cat <- factor(d$cat, levels = unique(d$cat[order(d$tot, d$cat)]))
    save_table(d, "gex_consensus_state_composition.tsv")
    withcap(sbar(d, paste0("Cell-state make-up of the ", nrow(top), " largest consensus clusters"),
                 "Fraction of cells", height = max(440, 26 * nrow(top) + 160), colors = state_cols(gx$annot), legend_title = "Cell state"),
            "Cell states of the largest consensus clusters",
            paste("Each bar sums to 100% of the cluster's TCR+ cells (count in brackets), coloured by state.",
                  "Clusters of a few cells can be one expanded clone; trust the make-up more for clusters",
                  "with many cells and several clonotypes (see the Consensus clustering table)."))
  }
} else if (have(gx_tcr)) note("No per-cell consensus labels were exported.")
```
